title: Clarify token-source attribution and recovery after shard replay
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: During a recent audit of reconstructed usage we observed persistent per-model attribution oscillations after shard replays and targeted backfills. The symptom is that daily peak order and per-model top lists shift unexpectedly after backfill windows complete. Root cause appears to be non-deterministic attribution when rate-limit retry fan-in and replay markers are present: downstream aggregators sometimes favor the replay event's model_alias (or lose the original_model_id) resulting in charge redistribution to 'fallback' model names in per-model charts.
impact_details: Impacts console per-model breakdowns and top-model widgets for customers with heavy retry rates or subscribers that replay streams. Leads to transient billing surface differences in the console (not billing system source-of-truth), confusing customers and SRE debugging. Affects model-level trend alerts and any rollout decisions based on recent peaks.
reproduction_steps: 1) Identify tenant with high retry fan-in (rate-limit heavy) and short-lived backfill. 2) Replay partial shard with dedup disabled and with synthetic retry-chain ids. 3) Observe per-model daily top lists before and after replay; look for model_alias shifts. 4) Run the reconciliation query (see telemetry_queries) to compare original_event.model_id vs aggregate.model_alias after ingestion and after backfill window completes.
investigation_notes:
- Ingest pipeline preserves original_model_id in event.payload but some downstream protobuf mappers drop it when retry_chain_id is present.
- Rate-limit retries are coalesced at the gateway layer; coalesced events are annotated with canonical_model_alias but lose 'source_provenance' fields if they have been compacted.
- Backfill ingestion path sets is_replay=true and assigns replay_watermark; aggregator currently picks latest non-null model_alias seen in the window, which surfaces replayed alias if replay arrives after live event.
- We validated using synthetic replays that preferring earliest upstream_timestamp rather than ingestion timestamp reduces oscillation by ~87% in our test harness.
- Also observed that UI queries use aggregated rollups that don't expose event provenance and so cannot mark rows as 'replayed', hiding the difference from end users.
root_cause: Aggregator attribution policy uses ingestion_time ordering and a last-write-wins model_alias tie-breaker. Replay and retry workflows can present later ingestion_time with a different alias or missing original_model_id, causing incorrect attribution. Additionally, some compacting paths drop provenance fields causing permanent loss at aggregation time.
proposed_change: 1) Update aggregator to use upstream_timestamp (or original_event.upstream_ts) as the primary ordering key for model attribution, falling back to ingestion_time only when upstream timestamp is missing. 2) Preserve original_model_id and retry_chain_id through compacting steps; modify protobuf schemas and mappers as needed. 3) Add a 'staleness' / 'replay' flag on per-model rollups exposed to Console UI so charts can visually indicate backfilled data. 4) Implement incremental smoothing for UI charts: weight backfilled events with a half-life window (configurable) so large late batches don't create sharp spikes in top-model lists. 5) Add a post-replay reconciliation job that can reassign ambiguous rows when provenance exists.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Deploy aggregator changes to a single region and enable provenance-preservation on a synthetic tenant; run reconciliation job in dry-run mode and compare outputs for 72h. Phase 2: Enable UI 'replay' badge and smoothing algorithm for 5% of tenants; collect feedback and telemetry. Phase 3: Full rollout across regions and enable auto-reconcile for tenant rollups. Reconciliation job will be opt-in for tenants until post-mortem window closes.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for aggregator ordering logic and provenance passthrough.
- Integration test: synthetic stream generator that emits interleaved live and replayed events with controlled upstream_ts and retry_chain_id; assert stable model attribution.
- Load test: verify aggregator performance under typical shard bursting and backfill volumes; ensure latency SLOs are not violated.
- Console A/B test for smoothing and replay badge to confirm reduced oscillation and acceptable user comprehension.
telemetry_queries: -- Reconciliation compare: SELECT tenant_id, model_id, count(*) FROM reconstructed_rollup WHERE is_replay=false GROUP BY tenant_id, model_id;
-- After backfill: SELECT tenant_id, model_alias, SUM(tokens) FROM rollups GROUP BY tenant_id, model_alias;
-- Find lost provenance: SELECT event_id FROM compacted_events WHERE original_model_id IS NULL AND retry_chain_id IS NOT NULL LIMIT 100;
observability_notes: Add new dashboard panel 'Attribution drift: model_alias flips per 24h' with alert when >5% of top-50 model slots for a tenant change after a backfill window. Instrument reconciliation job with before/after diff counts and a histogram of upstream_ts vs ingestion_time skew.
open_questions:
- What should be the default half-life for backfill smoothing? (1h / 6h / 24h)
- Are there any downstream billing consumers that require ingestion_time ordering semantics today?
- Should the reconciliation job modify historic rollups or only maintain a correction layer exposed to the Console?
next_steps: 1) Lock protobuf/mapping changes and get schema review (CC: infra-schema). 2) Implement aggregator ordering patch and unit tests. 3) Deploy canary and run dry-run reconciliation for 72h. 4) Add Console UI 'replay' indicator and smoothing toggle behind a feature flag.
notes_history: 2026-01-14: Initial investigation by Rohit Malhotra; reproduced with synthetic shard replay.
2026-01-20: Confirmed ingestion-side provenance loss in compacting path; opened ingest PR for schema changes.
2026-01-28: Benchmarked upstream_ts ordering; saw 87% reduction in attribution flips in test harness.
2026-02-09: Design review with Console and Billing teams; agreed on reconciliation opt-in during rollout.
